column15: Confirmed via the producer's own site (Whyte & Mackay Ltd): "Blended Scotch Whisky created in honour of the Scottish Claymore sword"; the site states no peat/smoke character at all. Retailer/aggregator tasting notes (Whiskybase, Honest Booze Reviews, Dear Whisky) describe "a gentle smoky note" and "slightly smoky" -- corrected peatProfile from the seed's light to unknown per the no-retailer-only-positive-peat rule. Withheld peat proposal: light, per retailer tasting notes only -- not producer domain, not Islay.

Crolly Distillery (Irish: Croithlí), County Donegal; site confirms first licensed whiskey distillery in Donegal since the 1840s and first single malt whiskey from Donegal in 180 years. Reconfirmed directly on the official site this session: Sessile Oak and other tasting notes (vanilla, caramel, green apple, oak, black pepper, creme brulee) show no smoke/peat language anywhere. "Croithlí" is the Irish-language place name (fada accent); catalogue brand string drops it. Upgraded from low to high confidence.

Confirmed real and identifiable: Pivdenna Stepova Brovarnya "Drofa" (Southern Steppe Brewery/Distillery "Drofa"), Kherson, Ukraine; operates its own guralnya (still-house) under a 2024 craft-spirits license, double-distils small batches from beer/wine/malt in copper alembics, ages in oak barrels or on oak chips/cubes/planks, won craft-spirits awards 2024-2025 (incl. a "beer whiskey" category). No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere, kept unknown. FLAG FOR REVIEWER: two of the four sampled SKUs are named plain "Distillate" (no aging qualifier) while the other two say "Aged on American/Bourbon Oak Chips" -- worth confirming per-SKU whether the unqualified ones are matured whisky-style spirit or unaged white spirit.

Own-label of Gallery Spirits Company (gspirits.eu is the producer's own domain): "crafted and bottled in Scotland", described on-page as a Highland whisky. Range spans blend (3yr/7yr) and single malt (5yr/10yr) expressions, so defaultTypeName left empty. Peat corrected from the seed's unknown to light: the producer's own site states a "subtle peaty finish" (3yr), "soft, sweet smoky touch" (5yr) and "subtle peppery hint" (10yr) -- satisfies the producer-domain corroboration rule for a positive claim.

Made by Spirit of Yorkshire Distillery Ltd, Hunmanby (founded 2016, first release 2019, per Wikipedia's list of English distilleries). Reconfirmed directly on the official site this session: Flagship, Moscatel Sherry Cask, STR Red Wine Cask and Yorkshire Day 2026 tasting notes list only honey/vanilla/citrus/caramel/biscuit/fruit-cake descriptors, zero smoke/peat language across the whole range -- inferred none from that consistent absence, not an explicit "unpeated" statement. Upgraded from low to high confidence.

Identified producer/bottler as Pirrie & Craig Co. (per Whiskybase's brand listing and Wine-Searcher retail listings; 1970s-era export bottlings also attested at auction) -- an addition over the seed round, which found no producer. No official Pirrie & Craig website found and no peat/smoke-specific source located, so kept at low confidence; peatProfile=none remains only the own-label ordinary-blended-Scotch default, not brand-verified.

Corrected peatProfile from the seed's none to unknown: no page I opened states an unpeated house style specific to this whisky (the official site only names peat as one of Scotch's four base ingredients in general). Country still unconfirmed -- the official site tells the Scottish-emigrant-history story behind the name but never states where the liquid is actually made, and a retail listing (crystaldistillery.com) traces to Crystal Distillery, based in Estonia -- this raises rather than resolves the "Glen-" fake-Scottish-name concern the seed flagged (cf. the EU "Glen Buchenbach" case). Left blank rather than assumed Scottish.

J&B Rare, produced by Justerini & Brooks (Diageo); a blend of around 42 malt and grain whiskies, Speyside-led (Knockando as "heart malt", plus Auchroisk, Strathmill, Glen Spey -- all unpeated distilleries). The page opened this session gives tasting notes ("fresh, grassy and nutty... malt, spice, fruit salad and sweet grains") but states no peat/smoke level for the finished blend either way; kept unknown rather than inferred from the unpeated fingerprint malts alone. Confidence raised to high since name/kind/country/owner are all independently confirmed.

Producer identified: King's Family Distillery, Pigeon Forge, Tennessee (opened 2018) -- confirmed via its own official product listing, which matches all four sampled names: King's Bourbon is sold at both 87 and 107 proof ("King's 107"), King's Wheated Bourbon 100 proof ("King's Wheated"), King's Rye ("King's Rye") and King's Ryeconic ("King's Ryeconic"). Range spans bourbon, wheated bourbon and rye, so defaultTypeName left empty. Site mentions "signature smoky tobacco" as a bourbon tasting note but never peat; American-whiskey category default (unpeated) applies. Kind corrected from blend to distillery (a real, named, operating craft distillery, not a sourced/undisclosed-parent label).

Confirmed via the brand's own official site: produced by James B. Beam Distilling Co., Clermont, Kentucky. Kind corrected from blend to brand and parentSlug set to jim-beam (already live), matching the Baker's/Basil Hayden's convention used elsewhere in the knowledge base. Range now also includes a rye, so defaultTypeName left empty. Bourbon/rye is categorically unpeated; no smoke/peat mentioned on the official site.

Producer identified: Helios Distillery, Nago, Okinawa, Japan (primarily a rum/awamori producer that also makes whisky under the "Kura" brand) -- confirmed via a page opened this session plus multiple consistent third-party listings for all three sampled names (Kura Rum Cask Finish Malt = "Kura The Whisky"; Kura White Oak = the ex-bourbon/American-white-oak-aged expression; Kura the Classic). New parentSlug row "helios" added. Peat: several third-party reviews describe the malt as heavily peated with Hokkaido peat before blending with unpeated malt and rum-cask finishing, but neither attempt to open a producer-domain page succeeded this session (helios-syuzo.co.jp and masterofmalt.com both blocked/403), and the one page that did open (sipjapan.com) mentions no peat at all -- kept unknown. Withheld peat proposal: medium, per https://www.nomunication.jp/2018/03/13/review-helios-kura-rum-cask/ (third-party review only).

Owner confirmed this session (the seed round only recalled this unverified): MacDuff International Ltd, a Glasgow blender founded 1992, which acquired Lauder's (plus Grand Macnish and Islay Mist) from Allied Distillers. Lauder's dates to 1834 and is "a blend of Highland, Lowland, and Speyside malts" per the cited page -- no Islay malt named and no peat/smoke mentioned, supporting peatProfile=none over the seed's unknown.

Country confirmed this session (blank in the seed): "distilled and matured in Ireland for The Old Carrick Mill Distillery, Derrylavan, County Monaghan" per the cited launch article. "May-Loag" spelled with a fada (May-Lóag) folds to the same normalized key. The four sampled expressions (Diamond/Elegance/Oriel/Triple Wood) are a blend of malt and grain finished in varied casks; none of them is the brand's separately-sold "May-Loag Peated Irish Whiskey", so peatProfile=none is set for this sampled range specifically. FLAG FOR REVIEWER: a "May-Loag Peated" SKU, if ever matched to this producer, would incorrectly inherit none and would need its own name-pattern rule -- not added here since no source confirming its exact peat intensity could be opened this session.

Reconfirmed directly on the official site this session: Belfast Distillery Company, Belfast, Northern Ireland (heritage dating to 1776); "a blend of select malt and grain whiskies, matured in ex-bourbon oak barrels". countryCode kept as IE per the island-of-Ireland whiskey-category convention -- the closed country list has no separate Northern Ireland code. No peat/smoke mentioned. Upgraded from low to high confidence.

Producer identified and confirmed via its own official site: Campbell Meyer & Company Ltd, East Kilbride, Scotland. Single malts from major distilling regions married with aged grain whisky; no peat/smoke mentioned in the producer's own tasting notes ("hay, malted barley, tangy citrus, roasted almonds, toffee, raisins"). Upgraded from low to high confidence.

MAJOR CORRECTION from the seed's peat=none: Micil Distillery's own official site describes peat/smoke across all four sampled expressions -- Inverin ("great balance of peat and charred wood smoke"), Earls Island ("hints of soft turf smoke from ex-peated whiskey casks"), Madeira Island ("light sweet peat smoke"), Long Walk ("a peated whiskey blend" with "soft peat smoke"). Connemara turf/peat is explicit brand heritage (the founder's family poitin-distilling background). Set to light for the house baseline given the consistently gentle/balanced wording, for a positive claim confirmed on the producer's own domain. Independent craft distillery, Galway (opened 2016, first legal Galway distillery in 100+ years); range spans small-batch/pot-still/blend styles so defaultTypeName stays empty.

Reconfirmed directly on the official site this session: independent craft distillery, Newport, Kentucky, distils/ages/bottles all of its own spirits (Bourbon, Rye, Single Malt Whiskey, Gin) -- an even wider range than the seed noted, reinforcing that defaultTypeName stays empty. No peat/smoke mentioned; bourbon/rye/American single malt is not a peated tradition here. Upgraded from low to high confidence.

Confirmed identity/producer this session (Wemyss Malts, Fife) via scotchwhisky.com/whiskypedia, reachable this session where the seed round's attempts all failed. Peat corrected from a vague "flag as likely heavy" to a properly withheld claim: independent sources agree the character is moderate/balanced, not extreme -- "peat plays a supporting role to exotic spices, moss and dark fruits" (scotchwhisky.com), 16 constituent malts "not all from Islay", "not an in-your-face blast of peat" (Scotch Noob review). A Wemyss Malts own-domain product page exists (wemyssmalts.com/products/peat-chimney-70cl-1) but its TLS handshake failed on every attempt this session, so it could not be opened directly. Withheld peat proposal: medium, per https://scotchwhisky.com/whiskypedia/2820/peat-chimney/ -- kept unknown pending an openable producer-domain source.

Reconfirmed this session: curated range of undisclosed single malts from Islay, launched 2009 by Sukhinder Singh/Elixir Distillers (then Speciality Drinks). Widely and consistently reported across independent reviews to be sourced from Caol Ila and described as "classic heavily-peated... salty and peaty" alongside a "balanced"/"elegant" house style -- kept heavy per the seed, corroborated rather than contradicted; region=islay independently satisfies the positive-peat gate regardless of exact intensity. Source distillery still deliberately left blank per the undisclosed-label rule.

Reconfirmed directly on the brand's own official site this session: Eire Born Spirits (Conor McGregor), Irish whiskey, triple-distilled blend of grain and single malt, minimum 4 years in charred ex-bourbon barrels. No peat/smoke mentioned; vanilla/honey/toasted-wood notes only. Upgraded from low to high confidence.

Peat upgraded from the seed's cautious "light, not confirmed" to a properly gate-qualifying claim: Douglas Laing's own official product page (opened this session) describes it as "soft and rather sweet peat paralleled with smoke" -- producer-domain corroboration for a positive claim. Blend of single malts from Islay, Arran, Jura, Orkney "(amongst others)"; formerly named Rock Oyster.

bottlerSlug corrected from the seed's old-malt-cask to hunter-laing: confirmed this session via Hunter Laing's own official site that Scarabus is its own standalone collection/brand, not a sub-label of Old Malt Cask. Single malt from an undisclosed Islay distillery, launched 2019 for Feis Ile alongside the opening of Hunter Laing's Ardnahoe distillery. Peat described on the producer's own domain as "sweet Islay peat smoke" / "signature sweet, peaty Scarabus profile" -- balanced rather than dominant, keeping the seed's medium (not heavy); both producer domain and Islay independently satisfy the gate.

New row for kura. Est. 1961, Nago, Okinawa, Japan; primarily an awamori and rum producer (Helios Shuzo) that also distils whisky, sold under the "Kura" brand. Multi-category distillery (rum, awamori, whisky), so no single defaultTypeName or peatProfile is asserted at this level.
